title: Chief of Staff / CEO office in a scale-up
why: You work directly on the CEO's priorities: strategy, board prep, special projects. Often open to ex-consulting interns and grads, and a common bridge into corporate strategy.
examples: French scale-ups listed on Welcome to the Jungle and Station F

title: Internal strategy consulting teams
why: Large groups run in-house consulting teams that hire like consulting firms but keep you inside one company, with good exit routes into strategy roles there.
examples: BNP Paribas CIB Consulting & Transformation (live offer in the Offers tab)

title: Open innovation and corporate venturing
why: Ties directly to your interest in open innovation: scouting start-ups, running partnerships and pilots for big corporates. You already applied to Impulse Partners in this space.
examples: Open-innovation consultancies and the venture arms of energy and automotive groups

title: Energy-transition strategy consulting
why: Strategy boutiques that only work on energy transition and climate. Your CSR ash-recovery project at AFOCO is a real talking point there.
examples: Enea Consulting, Carbone 4, energy practices of tier-2 firms

title: Pricing and commercial strategy
why: A strategy niche with heavy client contact in luxury, consumer and pharma. Lets you use your sales internship in Madrid alongside your strategy master.
examples: Simon-Kucher (live offer in the Offers tab)

title: Strategy for investors (commercial due diligence)
why: Strategy consulting for private-equity funds: market studies on short, intense deals. Good training and a route into PE value-creation roles.

title: VIE in a strategy or business-development team
why: 12–24 months abroad with a French group, tax-free allowance and real responsibility. Your Singapore and Australia experience makes you credible for Asia-Pacific posts.
examples: Euronext – Nord Pool Strategy Business Analyst VIE (Offers tab)

title: Rotational graduate programmes with a strategy track
why: You rotate through 2–3 roles before choosing, with one rotation in strategy. Safer bet than waiting for a single strategy opening.
examples: Renault Group (Strategy, Internal Consulting & Partnerships track)

title: PE performance improvement intern at Alvarez & Marsal (Paris, Jan/Mar 2027 start)
why: Private-equity value creation means working on companies after the deal: building value-creation plans, finding cost, margin, cash and growth levers, and producing board-level recommendations. That uses the same strategy toolkit as consulting, with more operational impact than due diligence alone. This 6-month Paris internship (posted 20 Aug 2026) offers a January or March 2027 start, which fits your end-of-studies window, and lists Spanish as a plus, which suits your Madrid sales experience.
examples: Alvarez & Marsal PEPI, Seven2 value creation team, Ardian Buyout operating team, Eurazeo portfolio performance, PAI Partners, Kéa & Partners PE practice

title: Economic consulting firms
why: Economic consultancies support competition authorities, lawyers and companies on mergers, market definition, pricing and regulation. The work is strategy analysis applied to high-stakes cases, and it is a parallel track that business-school students often overlook. In Europe they hire interns in the final year of studies, and your multi-country experience (Singapore, Madrid, Australia) is useful for cross-border cases. Expect a quantitative screening, so put your most analytical work first, such as the AFOCO ash-recovery business case.
examples: Compass Lexecon, Oxera, Microeconomix (Deloitte), Frontier Economics, RBB Economics, Charles River Associates, Analysis Group, NERA

title: Circular-economy business model strategist
why: Your AFOCO project on turning industrial ash into a resource is exactly what these roles do at scale: redesigning business models around reuse, recovery and take-back so that waste becomes a revenue stream (shared value in practice). You will find them in the strategy or circularity teams of corporates, in specialist consultancies and in foundations that advise multinationals. Few strategy graduates can show hands-on waste-valorisation experience, so you would stand out.
examples: Ellen MacArthur Foundation, Circulab, Citeo, Veolia strategy team, Suez, Back Market, Institut National de l'Économie Circulaire (INEC), Quantis

title: Decarbonisation strategy intern at Dassault Systèmes (Vélizy)
why: This is corporate strategy applied to a climate problem: benchmarking market practice, contributing to the group's decarbonisation strategy and leading internal working groups on carrying it out. Your AFOCO project gives you a real example of turning an environmental issue into a business case, and your interest in shared value fits. The offer was posted on 9 Oct 2026 and showed an active apply button on 2 Nov, though the page gives no start date, so check that it suits your 2027 calendar.

title: Transformation office and Project & Change Office analyst
why: Large groups set up small central teams to steer their biggest change programmes: governance, steering committees, risk tracking, change management and reporting to senior leaders. It is close to consulting work done from the inside, so your project-lead experience at AFOCO and your strategy Master both count, and it gives you a clear view of how strategy gets executed. Danone has a live January 2027 internship in Paris of this type.
examples: Danone DBS Project & Change Office (live, Paris, January 2027), Pernod Ricard Tech Transformation Office (past offer), International Chamber of Commerce Transformation department (past offer)

title: Expert networks: client-service associate
why: Expert networks connect consultants and investors with industry specialists for their strategy projects, so you see what strategy teams are working on across sectors. Your sales internship in Madrid and your languages are real assets, because the job is mostly phone-based, target-driven and multilingual, which also means it is less analytical than consulting. AlphaSights has a French-speaker intake for London closing on 20 Nov 2026 (check your UK right to work), and its German-speaker posting lists starts from January to September 2027.

title: European Commission Blue Book traineeship
why: This paid five-month traineeship places young graduates in Commission departments, agencies and Cabinets, so you could work on policy strategy rather than company strategy, for instance on industry, circular economy or trade. It would suit you after graduation, as a bridge year or as a public-sector line on a corporate-strategy CV, and your three languages help. Applications for the October 2027 session run from 15 Feb to 12 Mar 2027.
examples: European Commission departments, Commissioners' Cabinets, European External Action Service, EU executive agencies
